learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to replace boring, repeating nouns with pronouns and show ownership using possessive adjectives!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Pronouns are amazing shortcut words! Instead of saying 'Rohan ate Rohan's apple because Rohan was hungry', we use pronouns to say 'Rohan ate his apple because he was hungry'.
These are special describing words that sit right in front of a noun to show who owns it. Words like 'my', 'your', 'our', 'his', 'her', and 'their' are possessive adjectives!
A pronoun stands alone (The book is MINE), but a possessive adjective always needs a noun friend to sit next to (This is MY book). Do not mix them up!

fun_activity.title: 🔄 The Switcheroo Game
fun_activity.instructions: Write a short paragraph about your best friend using their name in every single sentence. Then, rewrite it by replacing their name with the correct pronouns!

quick_recap: ⭐ Pronouns replace nouns so our sentences do not sound repetitive and boring.
⭐ Possessive adjectives like 'my' or 'their' must always sit directly before a noun to show who it belongs to.
